subject: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up / FintechCo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up / FintechCo

Hi Samantha — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call:

What we heard:
- You want to validate whether an open/compatible model can meet your account-summary and transaction-classification needs at 200ms median latency for single-turn queries.
- Key success metrics: JSON-schema compliance for structured outputs (esp. account balances and transaction groups), <=2% field-level regression on precision/recall vs current baseline, and a cost target aligned with your monthly budget estimate.
- Operational asks: deterministic function/tool calling behavior (retries, idempotency), audit logs for outputs, and an SLA for inference latency on Dedicated if needed.

Agreed next steps (we can run these for you):
1) We will share recommended model variants and a short benchmark report tailored to your prompt set.
2) We’ll run an initial eval on your sample prompts and JSON schema to measure schema compliance, field-level F1, and regression risk.
3) We’ll provide a suggested prompt set and a test harness (you can run locally or let us run on Redwood Dedicated).
4) Tech follow-up to cover function-calling behavior: retries, idempotency tokens, and how Redwood logs structured outputs for audits.

Can you share: (a) a canonical JSON schema for the account summary output, (b) 50-100 sample prompts (if you have) or a short dataset, and (c) any hard constraints on latency vs cost? I’ve attached a small example prompt set to illustrate the format.

We’ll target initial eval results by EOD 2026-08-05, unless you prefer we run a quicker smoke test first.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: fintech_sample_prompts.json (sample prompts and expected JSON output stubs)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: QA Team <qa@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up / FintechCo

Thanks Marissa — this looks great. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) Model recommendations: we care about both quality and cost. Are you recommending quantized variants for this workload? We have a minimum latency requirement on mobile-facing endpoints.
2) Quality regression concerns: our legal/compliance team will want to see deterministic output for reconciliation and audit — how do you quantify risk of silent regressions when switching model variants?
3) Function-calling: we use the function-calling path to produce structured JSON that downstream services consume. We need guidance on retry semantics (at-most-once vs at-least-once) and idempotency tokens for stateful operations.

I’m attaching our canonical schema for the account summary output (account_summary_schema.json) and a small sample of 40 prompts that map to production cases.

If you could also include an estimate of how many eval tokens this will consume (so we can budget) that would be helpful.

—Samantha
VP Product, FintechCo

Attachments: account_summary_schema.json

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up / FintechCo

Hi Samantha — thanks for the schema and sample prompts, very useful. Quick technical plan and recommendations below.

Model recommendations (initial):
- redwood-compat-4x-q8 (quantized 8-bit): best cost/latency tradeoff for high throughput. Good starting point for smoke tests.
- open-xl-3b-fp16: higher-quality FP16 variant for head-to-head on edge cases where we see schema mismatch.
- fallback policy: if schema compliance drops below 95% we recommend automatic fallback to the FP16 variant for that route.

Benchmark links and initial numbers:
- Preliminary benchmark report: https://redwood-inference.internal/benchmarks/fintechco-model-fit-2026-07 (contains medians and 95th pct latencies on V100/A10-equivalent)
- Expected token usage for a 50-prompt run: ~12k input tokens + ~8k expected output tokens per run (estimate depends on truncation). We’ll give a detailed token-count estimate per prompt set in the report.

Eval plan for JSON-schema compliance and function-calling behavior:
1) Schema compliance: run the prompts and validate outputs against account_summary_schema.json. Metrics: overall schema pass rate, per-field F1/precision/recall, and error taxonomy (type mismatch, missing fields, unexpected enum values).
2) Structured output stability: run 3 rounds of the same prompts with controlled temperature/decoding to measure variance. We’ll report stability delta and identify prompts with high flaky outputs.
3) Function-calling semantics and retries: our recommendation:
   - For idempotent operations (read-only queries), use at-least-once with response dedup keys at the application layer.
   - For state-change operations, use an idempotency token passed through the tool-call metadata and enforce server-side dedup using request hashes.
   - Retry window: we recommend exponential backoff with jitter and bounded retries (max 3) for transient infra errors; do not retry on explicit schema-validation failures.

Test harness and links:
- Eval harness (you can run or we can run): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-id/fintech-eval-harness (contains the runner, prompt sets, and a JUnit-style result collector).
- We’ll attach a short PDF with the model recommendations and the initial schedule.

Next steps:
- We’ll run an initial 50-prompt pass using redwood-compat-4x-q8 and report schema pass rates by EOD 2026-08-05.
- If you prefer, we can run the FP16 variant in parallel for a smaller subset to quantify regression risks.

Let us know if you want us to proceed with running the evals from our side (we can do it on Dedicated or Hosted depending on confidentiality).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Applied ML — Evaluation
Redwood Inference

Attachments: model_recommendations_fintechco.pdf

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@fintechco.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: QA Team <qa@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up / FintechCo

Thanks — that plan works for us. Please go ahead and run the initial 50-prompt pass on redwood-compat-4x-q8 and share the schema pass-rate + per-field F1 by EOD today.

On retries: we’ll use idempotency tokens for state-change calls; for read-only endpoints we’ll surface dedup keys in the consumer to handle occasional duplicates.

If any of the runs hit schema pass < 92% please pause and flag to our QA before auto-fallback.

—Samantha
VP Product, FintechCo
